root_cause: _get_multidict_value() calls values.getlist(alias) whenever is_sequence_field(field) is true and values is an ImmutableMultiDict/Headers. For Json[list[str]] pydantic stores annotation=list[str] (Annotated stripped) with metadata=[Json()], so the field looks like a sequence; getlist wraps the raw JSON string in a list and pydantic's Json validator rejects a list ('JSON input should be string, bytes or bytearray').
best_solution: Add helper _is_json_field(field) = any(type(item) is Json for item in field.field_info.metadata) (import Json from pydantic) and in _get_multidict_value only use getlist() when the field is a sequence AND not a Json field; otherwise values.get(alias). Works because Json[T] expands to Annotated[T, Json()] and FieldInfo moves the Json() INSTANCE into .metadata while .annotation becomes the bare T; checking type(item) is Json on metadata is the only reliable signal. One choke point fixes Form, Query and Header (all multidicts); Cookie already used a plain dict.
acceptable_alternatives: isinstance(item, Json) over field.field_info.metadata; placing the same check inside is_sequence_field would also work but changes semantics for other callers (body/OpenAPI). Checks on field_info.annotation for Annotated/Json, 'Json in metadata', or 'arg is Json' do NOT work (annotation is already stripped; metadata holds an instance whose __eq__ is type(other) is type(self), so Json == Json() is False).
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_json_type.py: test_form_json_list, test_query_json_list, test_header_json_list, test_cookie_json_list; each endpoint takes Annotated[Json[list[str]], Form()/Query()/Header()/Cookie()] and must return 200 with ['abc','def'] when sent json.dumps(['abc','def']). Module-level Form route requires python-multipart installed at collection time.
locating_signals: Statement quotes the exact line 'value = values.getlist("items")' vs 'values.get("items")' and says 'treated it as a sequence field'; grepping getlist( / is_sequence_field lands on _get_multidict_value in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py. Function not named, but the snippet is a near-verbatim grep key. Statement also hints metadata: 'metadata attribute does not exist in Pydantic v1's FieldInfo'.
our_outcome_summary: v4/v6/v7/v8 all FAIL in the Kaggle env, and every failure is an ERROR collecting tests/test_json_type.py: 'RuntimeError: Form data requires "python-multipart" to be installed' raised at route definition. The env lacks python-multipart, so even the gold patch cannot pass. Our patches were also wrong on the merits: v6 was closest (right function, right metadata idea) but tested 'Json in field.field_info.metadata', which is False because metadata holds a Json() instance. v4 edited is_sequence_field, v7 and v8 edited shared.field_annotation_is_sequence, and all three looked for Annotated/Json on field_info.annotation (already stripped to list[str]) or used 'arg is Json' / __name__ == 'Json' on an instance. That is a no-op, so the bug remains. All four also left stray repro/test files (test_json_form*.py, repro.py, reproduce_issue.py). Pod runs took 112-214s and 63-109 calls.
generalizable_lesson: When a fix depends on detecting a library marker type (pydantic Json, Annotated metadata, typing wrappers), first print how the library actually stores it at runtime, e.g. FieldInfo.from_annotation(X).annotation/.metadata, and match on that object with isinstance or type(x) is. Do not reason from the source-level spelling. If the end-to-end repro cannot run because an optional dependency is missing, unit-test the changed helper directly on a constructed object instead of skipping verification. Before you finish, confirm the repro actually flips from failing to passing, then delete the scratch repro files.
